hook_text: A painted eland with crossed legs that unlocked the meaning of rock art.
clip_script: The Drakensberg, KwaZulu-Natal. An hour's hike to Game Pass Shelter. On the sandstone wall, eland, painted in ochre, clay and charcoal, by San artists. Tens of thousands of paintings fill these mountains, a World Heritage Site since 2000. One dying eland, legs crossed, with a part-human figure holding its tail, helped researchers understand the art: healers in trance, drawing on the eland's power. Rock art is fragile. Never touch it. Never wet it.
visual_style: Whiteboard mountain shelter, an eland being painted stroke by stroke, then a dancing healer, then a no-touch sign.
mood: Quiet and reverent, like entering a sacred place.
pacing: Slow hike up, a long pause at the paintings, then a firm safety note.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make a respectful copy of an eland painting.
